hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? have you ever felt lonely in a room full of people?
options: then you’re in good company. listen to this one.
then you know. this story knows too.
good. keep this one for a friend who does.

steps.line: In Matthew’s Gospel, on the night before he died, Jesus ate a last supper with his friends, then walked out with them into the dark.
They came to an olive garden called Gethsemane. He took three close friends, Peter, James and John, a little further in.
“My soul is very sorrowful,” he told them. “Stay here, and keep watch with me.”

steps.q: Jesus had crowds who followed him. Why ask just three friends to stay awake?
o: He needed guards for the garden
On his hardest night, he didn’t want to be alone
He was testing who was strongest
steps.why: Even he wanted someone near. Asking for company isn’t weakness.

steps.line: He went a little further, fell on his face, and prayed, alone.

steps.q: He comes back to his three friends, and they’re asleep. What does he do?
o: Wakes Peter: not even one hour?
Wakes them, angry, and sends them home
Prays aloud until they wake up
steps.why: Matthew 26:40: “Could ye not watch with me one hour?” A hurt question, to Peter, who had just sworn he’d never leave him.

steps.line: He came back, and found them asleep.
“Could you not watch with me one hour?” he said to Peter. Then, gently: “The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”

steps.q: Matthew says Jesus went back to pray a third time. What did he pray?
steps.why: Matthew 26:44: “saying the same words again.” Even Jesus didn’t find new words that night. Sometimes the same words are all there is.

steps.line: Today: 2 a.m., the whole building asleep. You’re not the only one awake with something heavy. Not even close.
steps.label: today

steps.q: The name Gethsemane comes from Hebrew or Aramaic words. What does it mean?
steps.why: Gat shemanim: an oil press, where olives are crushed. Many readers feel the name fits the night.

say: here’s what i love. the gospel doesn’t hide it. on his hardest night, jesus felt alone, and he said so, out loud, to his friends.

many christians take deep comfort here: loneliness doesn’t mean god has left. jesus knew it from the inside. and near the start of the bible, the first thing called not good is a person alone. you were made for company.

steps.q: Why might the Gospel writers keep this in, with Jesus’s own closest friends falling asleep?
o: Even close friends fail, and are loved
To show Jesus never needed them
steps.why: It’s honest. If even he felt alone in a garden full of friends, you’re in good company. And these same friends became the first leaders of the Church.

today.say: jesus didn’t hide it. he told his friends. today, if something heavy is keeping you up, tell one person, even in one line: rough night. if you like, you can tell god too, in your own words, the way he did. that part is your choice. and if it ever feels like danger, call 988 in the united states, or your local emergency number.
options: good. one line is enough. the room is full.
i’m glad. maybe be the friend who stays awake for someone else.
